chapter_theme: The kaathai of spring: spring arrives over the Tamil land as the herald and army of Kama, Madhavi, left by the sulking Kovalan, plays the yaazh and writes him a letter on a flower leaf, and Kovalan refuses it, recalling every sign of her love as a dancing woman's role, so that the quarrel at the shore becomes the break that sends him back to Kannaki.

silappathikaram:8:1-13.reading: The young southern breeze, messenger born of the great sage of fertile Pothiyil, announces that sweet young spring, the delighting companion of king Maran, has come to the cool land whose Tamil bounds are cut by the hill of the tall god and the sea of the bangled goddess, where kings sit in Madurai, Uraiyur, Vanji and Puhar; and as if the army of the makara-bannered youth were putting on its flawless array, the cuckoo, a soldier in that army, calls the command through the crowded groves.
silappathikaram:8:1-13.nuance: Spring arrives as a king's affair: a herald (தூதன்), an army (சேனை, படை), an order spoken by a soldier (பணிமொழி). The setting is the whole Tamil land, named by its two bounds and the capitals of all three crowns, not Puhar alone, so the season that will break Kovalan and Madhavi is announced as a law over every Tamil city. The breeze is 'born of the sage' of Pothiyil because the south wind blows from that hill.
silappathikaram:8:1-13.event: The southern breeze announces the coming of spring and the cuckoo calls in the groves.

silappathikaram:8:14-24.reading: Madhavi, whom Kovalan left without joining her after he sulked at the sea-sport on the flowering shore, goes in her longing up to the spring chamber on the high terrace, takes the court of saffron on her breasts, where the southern sea's pearls and the southern hill's sandal pay their dues, as her offering, takes up the yaazh of steady tradition and, lost in feeling, sings a sweet song.
silappathikaram:8:14-24.nuance: Line 15 gives Kovalan's leaving at the end of the Kaanal Vari as a sulk (ஊட) that would not end in union (கூடாது), a lover's quarrel; the narrator there (7:289) gave it as Kovalan's ஊழ்வினை rising to bear fruit. The epic so names two causes for one departure, fate and pique, and neither cancels the other. The pearls and sandal paying tribute (கடன் இறுக்கும்) to her breasts carry on the opening unit's language of kings and dues.
silappathikaram:8:14-24.event: Left by the sulking Kovalan, Madhavi climbs to her spring chamber and sings to the yaazh.
silappathikaram:8:14-24.unit_note: Boundary moved from 29|30 to 24|25: line 24 (மதுர கீதம் பாடினள் மயங்கி) closes the account of her going up and singing, and lines 25 to 44 are one run describing how she sits, tunes and plays.

silappathikaram:8:25-44.reading: Seated in the first of the nine postures, her right hand set to the yaazh's neck and four fingers of her left on the pegs, Madhavi, knowing the skill that removes the string faults named by the treatise, ties the fourteen strings from ulai to kaikkilai, tests the four relations of notes, listens to kural and ili, plays the scales of five and seven beginning and ending on ulai and on kural, the four kinds of marutham and the three movements, until in one outer measure the flowering creeper herself is lost in it.
silappathikaram:8:25-44.nuance: The catalogue is a performer's checklist, the same craft the yaazh player of 3:70-94 is praised for, now done alone by Madhavi for no audience. The modes she plays are the marutham ones; marutham is in Tamil poetics the landscape of the lovers' quarrel, so the music fits her situation without the poem saying so. All this control ends in மயங்கி: mastery tips into self-loss. Many terms (இணை கிளை பகை நட்பு, மூவகை இயக்கம், புறத்துஒரு பாணி) are technical and I read them only in outline.
silappathikaram:8:25-44.event: Madhavi tunes the yaazh, tests its notes and plays the marutham modes until she loses herself in the music.
silappathikaram:8:25-44.unit_note: Start moved from 30 to 25 with the change at 24|25 (see silappathikaram:8:14-24); the end at 44 (பூங்கொடி மயங்கி) is unchanged.

silappathikaram:8:45-55.reading: Bound up with champak, madhavi, tamaalam, karumugai, white jasmine with vetiver, red kazhuneer and kattigai flowers, Madhavi takes the curved white leaf of a ripe thaazhai, and, ready to send the royal letter that the whole world bows to by order of the one man whose single sceptre rules the earth with fragrant flower-arrows, she dips into the thick red lac and takes a pithigai bud as her stylus.
silappathikaram:8:45-55.nuance: The letter is called திருமுகம், the word for a king's writ, and Madhavi writes it 'by the order' (ஆணையின்) of Kama's 'single sceptre' (ஒருதனிச் செங்கோல்). The figure is love as sovereign, not a claim about kingship; but the epic that will turn on a bent sceptre in Madurai here gives a sceptre to desire, whose order Kovalan is about to refuse. Her own name, மாதவி, stands in the flower list at line 45.
silappathikaram:8:45-55.event: Madhavi takes a thaazhai leaf, red lac and a jasmine bud to write a letter to Kovalan.
silappathikaram:8:45-55.unit_note: Boundary moved from 60|61 to 55|56: line 55 (ஆணி கைக்கொண்டு) ends the preparation, and line 56 begins the words of the letter, which run to line 63 (அறிந்தீ மின்என).

silappathikaram:8:56-73.reading: Madhavi writes that young spring, the prince who joins every living being to its mate, and the moon born in the bud of evening are not kind: if joined lovers let time come between them, or parted lovers forget their partners, it is no wonder that love takes their lives with flower-arrows, so let them know it; she writes this with all sixty-four arts at her command yet in the unformed lisp of a lonely desire, then, pale with longing, calls Vasantamalai and bids her give Kovalan the flower garland with all its meaning and bring him back, and Vasantamalai gives it to him in the grain-market street.
silappathikaram:8:56-73.nuance: The letter is a warning in the plural and impersonal, not a plea: it never names Kovalan or herself, and puts the blame for delay on the lovers who let time divide them. Line 68 plays three ways on மாலை: the evening of her pain, Vasanta-maalai her messenger, and the flower maalai that carries the writing. Kovalan is found not at home but in the grain-market street.
silappathikaram:8:56-73.event: Madhavi writes her letter on the garland and sends Vasantamalai, who gives it to Kovalan in the grain-market street.

claims.claim: lovers who let time divide them, or who forget their partners when apart, deserve to have love take their lives

silappathikaram:8:56-73.unit_note: Start moved from 61 to 56 (see silappathikaram:8:45-55); end moved from 77|78 to 73|74: line 73 (கோவலற்கு அளிப்ப) closes the delivery, and line 74 begins Kovalan's answer, the catalogue of Madhavi's love-plays.

silappathikaram:8:74-93.reading: Kovalan answers by naming, one by one, the love-plays Madhavi has shown him: the glance of eyes meeting in love from a face like a sword; the play of coming when called and going when sent, showing her pearl smile; the inner play when, seeing his distress at evening, she hid her parrot speech, swan gait and peacock grace and came alone dressed as a serving maid; and the outer play when she danced outside with anklets wailing and girdle ringing, looking lovingly at his changed and wretched state.
silappathikaram:8:74-93.nuance: Each memory is given a technical name ending in வரி (கண்கூடு வரி, காண்வரிக் கோலம், உள்வரி, புன்புற வரி), the names of acted love in the dance treatise. Kovalan is recalling real tenderness, her coming to him disguised as a maid when he was low, but by filing each act under a genre of performance he turns their life together into a repertoire.
silappathikaram:8:74-93.event: Kovalan answers Vasantamalai by listing Madhavi's past shows of love as dance roles.
silappathikaram:8:74-93.unit_note: Start moved from 78 to 74 (see silappathikaram:8:56-73); the end at 93 (புன்புற வரியும்) is unchanged.

silappathikaram:8:94-110.reading: Kovalan goes on: the stirring play when, hearing her maids carry back his replies full of quarrel-making double meanings hidden within union, her grace drooped and her soft hair stirred; the play of careful telling when, parted from him, she told her own grief to his kin; the play of the dazed lover who told her state to whoever saw her; and the play of the lifted swoon when she fainted again and again before them and they raised her: since she is a dancing woman, he says, all of these were fitting achievements for her.
silappathikaram:8:94-110.nuance: Lines 109 and 110 are the verdict, and the verdict is a refusal (the next unit calls it மறுத்தது): ஆடல் மகள் names her by her calling and makes the calling the proof that her grief was art. The narrator had blamed the first break on Kovalan's ஊழ்வினை (7:289); this second break is in Kovalan's own words and names no fate, so the story lays the choice on him too. The judgment is answered later by Kovalan himself, who reads her second letter and says she is without fault and the fault is his (13:93-95).
silappathikaram:8:94-110.event: Kovalan refuses the letter, saying every sign of Madhavi's love was a role that suits a dancing woman.

claims.claim: a dancing woman's signs of love are performances of her art, not true feeling

silappathikaram:8:94-110.unit_note: Unit 94-118 split at 110|111: line 110 (பாடுபெற் றனஅப் பைந்தொடி தனக்குஎன) closes Kovalan's speech, and line 111 turns to Vasantamalai's return.

silappathikaram:8:111-118.reading: Grieving that the jewelled letter written on an ornamented leaf by the jewelled woman was refused, Vasantamalai, her heart wilted, hurries back and tells Madhavi, who says that though he will not come this evening they will see him in the morning, and lies on her flowered bed with a helpless heart, unable to rest.
silappathikaram:8:111-118.nuance: Her last words set evening against morning (மாலை ... காலை), and the morning she waits for does not bring him: the next kaathai has Kovalan at Kannaki's door. The 'helpless heart' (கையறு நெஞ்சம்) is a phrase her second letter will ask him to take away.
silappathikaram:8:111-118.event: Vasantamalai reports the refusal, and Madhavi lies sleepless, hoping to see Kovalan in the morning.
silappathikaram:8:111-118.unit_note: New unit from the split of 94-118 at 110|111 (see silappathikaram:8:94-110); it ends at the kaathai's akaval close, line 118 (மாதவி தான்என்).

silappathikaram:8:119-126.reading: Two closing venbas: the first says that with the red lotus opening, mango shoots trickling and the strong ashoka unfolding its buds, clustered young spring has come, and asks what will become today of the heart of the woman with spear-bright eyes; the second says that the cuckoo has proclaimed the formless one's command, 'all you who have sulked, unite', and bids the one who, troubled by the shore song, spurned the soft flower letter of her who joined in the long spring song, to see it.
silappathikaram:8:119-126.nuance: The second venba sets two songs against each other: the கானல் பாணி, the shore songs of 7 that started the quarrel, and the வேனல் பாணி, the spring song in which Madhavi wrote. I read அலந்தாய் as addressed to Kovalan, who refused the letter, but the line is compressed and the addressee is not named.

claims.claim: all lovers who have quarrelled must reunite, for that is the love god's command

links.note: At the end of the Kaanal Vari the narrator says Kovalan let go of Madhavi because his ஊழ்வினை rose to bear fruit (line 289); here the same departure is recalled as Kovalan sulking and leaving without union (கோவலன் ஊடக் கூடாது ஏகிய).
links.teaches: One act is given two causes a kaathai apart, past karma ripening and a lover's pique, so the epic's fate does not replace Kovalan's own temper but works through it.

links.note: Both letters are sent through Vasantamalai with the same formula for Madhavi's state (பசந்த மேனியள் படர் ..., line 68 here; 13:67-68), and in both she writes with her own hand.
links.teaches: The repeated wording marks the second letter as a rerun of the first, so the reader can see that what changes between a refused and an accepted letter is Kovalan's state, not Madhavi's message.

links.note: Here Kovalan refuses Madhavi's letter, filing her every sign of love as a dancing woman's role; reading her second letter in the forest he decides she is without fault and the fault is his (தன்றீ திலளென ... என்தீ தென்றே, 13:94-95).
links.teaches: Kovalan's verdict that a dancer's grief is only art is withdrawn by Kovalan himself once he is ruined and far away, so the story shows the judgment came from his sulk and not from anything in her.

links.note: The couplet says sulking is like salt, and drawing it out a little too long is like a little too much; Kovalan's sulk, begun at the shore, is here drawn out into a refusal of her letter.
links.teaches: Past the couplet's 'little too much' the quarrel stops being a spoiled sweetness and becomes a verdict on the beloved's whole nature, which is how a lovers' sulk turns into the epic's break.

gains.a: the refusal gains a measure by which it is an excess of an ordinary lovers' sulk rather than a reasoned judgment of Madhavi
gains.b: the couplet gains a case showing what the excess it warns of looks like, a rereading of all past tenderness as pretence, with a cost it does not name

links.note: In the akam poem the wife refuses the bard sent to plead for her husband because he is a deceiving philanderer (மாயப் பரத்தன்); here the man refuses the go-between sent by the courtesan because her love is a dancer's art.
links.teaches: The epic stages a marutham refusal of the go-between with the roles turned round, so that the charge of false love the convention lets the wife bring against the man is brought by the man against the courtesan.

gains.a: the scene gains its genre: Kovalan's answer is a வாயில் மறுத்தல், and its harshness reads as a convention used against Madhavi
gains.b: the poem gains a view from the other side of the same convention, where the one refused is the woman and the charge of deceit is shown, later in the story, to be wrong

links.note: Madhavi lies down saying that though he will not come in the evening she will see him in the morning (காலைகாண் குவம்); in the next kaathai Kovalan comes instead to Kannaki's door (கடைத்தலையான் வந்துநம் கோவலன்).
links.teaches: The morning Madhavi waits for is the morning Kovalan returns to his wife, so her hope and Kannaki's dream are the two ends of one night, and the courtesan's loss is the wife's recovery.

links.note: Madhavi lies with a helpless heart (கையறு நெஞ்சமொடு, line 116); her second letter ends asking Kovalan to take away the helpless heart (கையறு நெஞ்சம் கடியல் வேண்டும், 13:91).
links.teaches: The phrase carries one night's grief into the later letter, showing that what Madhavi asks of Kovalan there is to undo the state this refusal left her in.

links.note: The couplet says sulking is love's pleasure and its pleasure is to come together and embrace; the venba has the cuckoo proclaim love's command to all who have sulked (ஊடினீர்) to unite (கூடுமின்), and chides the one who spurned the letter.
links.teaches: The couplet's pleasure rests on a condition, that union follows, and the venba shows that condition failing even under love's own command, so the sulk the Kural treats as seasoning becomes the start of a separation.

gains.a: the venba's command gains a stated rule of love, so Kovalan's refusal is a breach of love's own order and not only of Madhavi's hope
gains.b: the couplet's closing condition பெறின், 'if one gets to', gains a case where one does not get to, and what follows then

new_concepts.gloss: young spring, the season of the love god's rule, when lovers are bidden to unite and the parted suffer most
new_concepts.label_source: the unit's own word (இளவேனில் lines 7, 57 and 121; the kaathai is named வேனில் காதை)

new_concepts.gloss: music: the lute, melody, mode and the sounds compared to them
new_concepts.label_source: the unit's own word (இசை, lines 34 and 43; யாழ் line 23); id as declared in silappathikaram ch008

new_concepts.gloss: dance-drama as a learned art, with its kinds, rules, gestures and accompanying music, performed before the king
new_concepts.label_source: my label for the dance roles named வரி and ஆடல் (lines 77, 89, 93, 101, 109); id as declared in silappathikaram ch004

source_issues: The kaathai has 126 lines in the core text but the edition's printed numbering ends at 115, so line numbers here (the kaathai's own, 1-126 as `show` prints them) differ from the printed ones.
Line 9 (இளங்கால் தூதன் இசைத்தனன் ஆதலின்) carries a repaired encoding flag (a TSCII leftover read as ூ); the repaired reading makes sense and I marked it as written.
Lines 109 (ஆயிழை.) and 115 (மாண்இழை.) end in a full stop in mid-sentence; the sense runs on into the next line in both, so I read through the stops.
The closing unit 119-126 holds two separate venbas (119-122 and 123-126) in one core unit; I marked it as one unit because boundaries may not move inside the venba block.

cast.role: son of the merchant Maasaathuvan, Kannaki's husband, who has left Madhavi after the quarrel at the shore
the dancer of Puhar with whom Kovalan lived
Madhavi's companion, who carries her letters to Kovalan
Kama, the god of desire, here also மாரன் and உருஇலான், the formless one
the young southern breeze from Pothiyil, herald of spring
the cuckoo, a soldier of Kama's army who proclaims his command
